exposure: place of delivery (health centre vs. home/traditional birth attendant)
mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 275 post-natal mothers attending primary healthcare centres in Ede, Nigeria.
finding: The study revealed good knowledge and practice of cord care among post-natal mothers in Ede, with delivery in a health centre predicting good knowledge, and vaginal delivery and being married predicting good cord care practice.
mod_finding: Mothers who had a vaginal delivery had significantly higher odds of good umbilical cord care practice compared to those who delivered by cesarean section.
